reception: Beyond the thesis, external reception runs largely through StreamIt itself: groups retargeting the language treat this paper's partitioning, layout, and communication scheduling as the reference compilation path. Huynh and colleagues mapped streaming applications onto multi-GPU systems, Wang and O'Boyle partitioned stream graphs with machine learning, and StreamX10 carried the approach to X10, while throughput-driven synthesis for pipelined multicores measured against it. The larger citation mass is more distant: the paper appears in many works as the example of compiling a stream language onto communication-exposed hardware, and a steady share cites its Raw results as evidence of what static orchestration can achieve. The StreamIt compiler infrastructure lives on in the bthies/streamit repository.
